day_shape: 77 items: Araghchi at BRICS in New Delhi rejecting any military solution, reported Fujairah maritime incident with UKMTO involvement, Trump-Xi summit covering Iran, seven UK parliamentary questions tabled on the Iran war, and heavy regime messaging on Strait of Hormuz control.

threads.label: Fujairah maritime incident reported
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press said a maritime incident occurred 38 nautical miles northeast of Fujairah, citing UKMTO, and claimed a ship was seized while berthing and moved toward Iranian waters. Separately, regime channels said a Japanese ship transited the Strait of Hormuz with Iranian permission after PM-level contact with Pezeshkian.

threads.label: Araghchi at BRICS New Delhi
threads.summary: Iranian FM Araghchi attended the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi, welcomed by India's Jaishankar, and told the gathering there is no military solution regarding Iran while announcing bilateral meetings with Brazil, Egypt, Malaysia, Russia and Cuba. Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post framed the forum as overshadowed by the US-Israeli war on Iran and as bringing Iran and the UAE together.

threads.label: Trump-Xi summit and China-Iran track
threads.summary: Trump and Xi met at Beijing's Great Hall of the People, with Iran on the agenda alongside trade and Taiwan arms sales. Iran International reported Tehran is looking to Beijing for guarantees in any future US deal, while Jerusalem Post reported Chinese companies have allegedly been routing clandestine arms to Iran via third countries.

threads.label: US-Iran nuclear track and ceasefire
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported US-Iran talks stalled after Tehran tried to skirt up-front nuclear concessions, while Jerusalem Post said US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing that Iran is "frighteningly close" to nuclear weapons. Jerusalem Post also reported the Trump administration is considering renaming its Iran military campaign — one option being "Operation Sledgehammer" — if the ceasefire collapses.

threads.label: Netanyahu UAE visit and Gulf strikes revealed
threads.summary: Netanyahu disclosed a secret visit to the UAE during the Iran war, with reports that Mossad and Shin Bet chiefs also travelled, and Iran's FM responded with threats to the UAE claiming Tehran knew of the trip. Reuters-sourced reporting via Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post said Saudi warplanes and Kuwait struck Iran-backed Shi'ite militias in Iraq during the war.

threads.label: UK Parliament Iran questions tabled
threads.summary: Seven written questions on Iran were tabled at Westminster, covering RAF Akrotiri ballistic-missile defence during HMS Dragon maintenance, treatment of Bahá'ís, alleged use of Belfast International airport for operations against Iran, and impacts of the war on fertiliser, food security and heating oil. A Presidential Determination on NDAA section 1245(d)(4)(B)/(C) and a US Coast Guard Port Security Advisory revocation were also published in the Federal Register.

threads.label: Regime domestic war messaging
threads.summary: Iranian judicial authorities said assets of 47 and 53 alleged collaborators with Israel were confiscated in Hamadan, while the Education Minister said final exams would be held two weeks after the war ends and office hours from Saturday would run 6am–1pm. Khamenei's office posted donation channels for war-affected citizens and a "unity" message, and IRIB carried Admiral Siiari saying "America will be defeated in a war with Iran."

events.summary_en: Jerusalem Post: Houthis continue to expand their arsenal using new Iranian components in missiles. According to a report by the Conflict Armament Research (CAR) centre, the electronic components used in recent attacks were produced in the past two years, indicating that the supply networks for transferring equipment are strong and continuous, and Houthis are being supplied with new systems. Anti-ship, surface-to-air, and ballistic missiles are among these weapons, showing that Houthis now possess a wide range of advanced offensive capabilities.

events.title_en: Unity, a necessary condition for achieving 'Iran ever stronger'
events.summary_en: Unity, a necessary condition for achieving 'Iran ever stronger'. When our martyred leader took on the leadership, the Islamic Republic system was like a sapling that had received multiple wounds from enemies of Islam and Iran and had of course withstood them well. But when, after nearly 37 years, they departed from the seat of leadership of the nation, they left behind a blessed tree with solid roots and branches casting shade over important parts of the region and the world. The approach to achieving 'Iran ever stronger' passes through unity among different sections of society, which was repeatedly emphasised by them. Ayatollah Seyyed Mujtaba Hosseini Khamenei | 10 April 2026.
